plain_text:
More than 31% of U.S. adults experience
an anxiety disorder at some time in their lives.
semantic_text: More than 31% of U.S. adults experience an anxiety disorder at some time in their lives.

plain_text: SOURCE: NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MENTAL HEALTH
semantic_text: SOURCE: NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MENTAL HEALTH

plain_text:
The good news is that anxiety is treatable. Different
strategies to help manage your anxiety may involve
psychotherapy, medication, or both.
semantic_text: The good news is that anxiety is treatable. Different strategies to help manage your anxiety may involve psychotherapy, medication, or both.

plain_text:
■ Cognitive behavioral therapy, or CBT, which
teaches people different ways of thinking, behaving,
and reacting to situations to help them feel less
anxious or afraid
■ Exposure therapy, a type of CBT that helps people
confront fears so they can participate in activities they
have avoided
■ Acceptance and commitment therapy, which uses
strategies such as mindfulness and goal setting to help
people live fulfilling lives despite their anxiety
Medication doesn't cure anxiety, but it can help some people
manage their symptoms. Some may include:
semantic_text: ■ Cognitive behavioral therapy, or CBT, which teaches people different ways of thinking, behaving, and reacting to situations to help them feel less anxious or afraid ■ Exposure therapy, a type of CBT that helps people confront fears so they can participate in activities they have avoided ■ Acceptance and commitment therapy, which uses strategies such as mindfulness and goal setting to help people live fulfilling lives despite their anxiety Medication doesn't cure anxiety, but it can help some people manage their symptoms. Some may include:

plain_text:
■ Anti-anxiety medications, which may reduce the
symptoms of anxiety, panic attacks, or extreme fear
and worry
■ Antidepressants, which can improve the way
the brain uses certain chemicals that control mood
or stress
■ Beta blockers, which can relieve physical symptoms
of anxiety such as rapid heartbeat, shaking, trembling,
and blushing
semantic_text: ■ Anti-anxiety medications, which may reduce the symptoms of anxiety, panic attacks, or extreme fear and worry ■ Antidepressants, which can improve the way the brain uses certain chemicals that control mood or stress ■ Beta blockers, which can relieve physical symptoms of anxiety such as rapid heartbeat, shaking, trembling, and blushing

plain_text:
Other strategies can help you manage anxiety and make
treatment more effective. These include exercise, relaxation
techniques such as deep breathing or meditation, and lifestyle
changes such as limiting caffeine and alcohol and getting
enough sleep.
semantic_text: Other strategies can help you manage anxiety and make treatment more effective. These include exercise, relaxation techniques such as deep breathing or meditation, and lifestyle changes such as limiting caffeine and alcohol and getting enough sleep.

plain_text:
A strong social support system is also important, whether
it's through talking to friends and family or joining a
support group.
semantic_text: A strong social support system is also important, whether it's through talking to friends and family or joining a support group.

plain_text:
Remember, feeling anxious sometimes is normal. But if
your symptoms last a long time, get worse, or interfere with your
day-to-day life, it may be a sign of an anxiety disorder. If you or
someone you know is experiencing symptoms of anxiety disorders,
reach out to a health care provider. Help is available, and you don't
have to face your anxiety alone.
semantic_text: Remember, feeling anxious sometimes is normal. But if your symptoms last a long time, get worse, or interfere with your day-to-day life, it may be a sign of an anxiety disorder. If you or someone you know is experiencing symptoms of anxiety disorders, reach out to a health care provider. Help is available, and you don't have to face your anxiety alone.

plain_text:
Learn more about anxiety and get helpful tips for managing it.
Check out these videos from the National Institute of
Mental Health.
